title: Find Polygon With the Largest Perimeter
statement:
`nums` holds positive integers that you may use as side lengths, each entry at most once. A polygon needs at least 3 sides, and a set of side lengths forms one exactly when its longest side is strictly shorter than the total of all its other sides. The perimeter is the total of all the side lengths.

Choose entries of `nums` that form a polygon and return the largest perimeter you can reach. If no choice of entries forms a polygon, return `-1`.
notes:
## Intuition

Suppose some side `x` is the longest one of the polygon. Adding any other unused side no longer than `x` only makes the "other sides" total bigger, so the polygon stays valid and its perimeter grows. So for a fixed longest side, the best choice is to take **every** entry that sorts before it. After sorting, each candidate is a prefix of the array, and the longest valid prefix wins. Trying every subset would cost O(2ⁿ).

## Approach

1. Sort `nums` in ascending order.
2. Keep `prefix`, the sum of all entries before index `i`, and `best = -1`.
3. For each `i`, the prefix ending at `i` is a polygon when it has at least 3 sides (`i >= 2`) and `prefix > nums[i]`. Then its perimeter `prefix + nums[i]` is the best so far, because prefixes only get bigger.
4. Add `nums[i]` to `prefix` and continue. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

Sorted `nums = [5, 5, 5]`. At `i = 0` and `i = 1` there are too few sides; `prefix` becomes 5, then 10. At `i = 2`, `prefix = 10 > 5`, so `best = 10 + 5 = 15`, and that is the answer.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n): the sort dominates; the scan is linear.
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort.

## Pitfalls

- The check is strict: `[1, 2, 3]` is not a polygon because `1 + 2` equals `3`.
- Do not stop at the first failing prefix; a later, longer prefix can succeed again (`[1, 1, 2, 3]` works even though `[1, 1, 2]` does not).
- Sums reach about 10^14, so typed languages need a 64-bit total.
- A prefix must have at least three sides, which is why `i >= 2` is part of the test.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `prefix` | sum of the sorted entries before index `i` |
| `best` | largest valid perimeter found so far, or `-1` |
| `i` | index of the side tried as the longest |

narration.2: Sort ascending so every candidate polygon is a prefix of the array.
narration.3: prefix will hold the sum of all sides before index i.
narration.4: No polygon found yet, so the answer starts at -1.
narration.6: Try each entry in turn as the longest side.
narration.7: With at least two smaller sides, the prefix is a polygon if their total beats nums[i].
narration.8: Its perimeter is the largest so far, since later prefixes only add length.
narration.10: Add this side to the running total for the next candidate.
narration.12: Return the largest perimeter found, or -1 if no prefix worked.
